STUDIO-OBS-014 AC-11: design note only in this wave unless @architect promotes it

ruling1_AC11_keyCustody.verdict: CUSTODY = HashiCorp Vault Transit (design-note option A), on the same platform Vault that Studio secret refs already target. Platform KMS (option B) is REJECTED for this delivery and stays a fallback only if Platform/SRE confirms Transit is unavailable. AC-11 is NOT promoted to implementation in OBS-014 (or 012A/012B). Delivery in 014 is the amended design note. The implementation becomes a follow-up story with a named entry gate.
verifiedFacts: Vault is the only external key/secret service this backend integrates. HashicorpStudioVaultProvider is a hand-written java.net.http client (no Spring Cloud Vault and no Vault SDK in build.gradle.kts). It authenticates with X-Vault-Token from a mounted token file, optionally sends X-Vault-Namespace, never follows redirects, bounds responses, and uses connect 2s / request 5s timeouts (application.yml:259-280).

The Vault adapter is default-off in every profile: studio.secrets.vault.provider is ${STUDIO_VAULT_PROVIDER:none} in application.yml, application-local.yml and application-dev.yml, and 'none' in application-test.yml. Tests select the fake provider. helm values.yaml:637-653 reads 'Real Vault KV v2 is implemented but explicitly off until the platform endpoint is connected'. values-prod.yaml and values-uat.yaml say 'THE VAULT IS STILL A STUB' and tie the credentialed pilot to ED-02, which is owned by the PUT Core platform and still open.

The observed/guided path already fails closed on Vault: GuidedProductionSessionAccess.java:105 and GuidedDispatchService.java:81 refuse with 503 VAULT_UNAVAILABLE. Transit therefore adds no new availability dependency to the replay path.

The repository has no KMS integration. The only KMS mention is object-store bucket encryption in docs/runbooks/studio-integrations.md:94, which is storage encryption and not a MAC/sign API available to this service.
Nowhere in the repository (backend, helm-chart, docs, ARCH.md, PRD.md) does any document say that Vault Transit is enabled on the platform Vault. The design note is right to call this unverified.
rationale: No new mandatory framework. Transit HMAC/verify is two HTTPS POSTs to the same Vault address with the same auth style. They reuse the existing bounded HTTP pattern of HashicorpStudioVaultProvider, so no SDK is added. Option B would add a cloud KMS client library and a second credential path.

One external dependency instead of two. Guided authoring and secret-ref replay already need Vault, so a Vault outage already stops them. KMS would add a second independent outage domain to every replay.
Same audit surface: Vault's audit device logs secret reads, and with Transit it would also log every HMAC/verify call. KMS would split the audit trail.
Trade-off accepted: binding to Vault couples this control to ED-02, which is not done. That is not a regression, because no credentialed or deployed observed replay may run before ED-02 anyway.
whyNotPromotedInto014: No environment can exercise the real provider today: Vault is off everywhere and Transit availability is UNCONFIRMED. If 014 implemented a fail-closed check now, every test would run against a fake. 014 would then claim a production control that has never met its production dependency, which is the 'fake prod claim' to avoid.

014 already carries T2 (AC-4/5/6, not started), the S3 window and the staged C2b unit. Adding a migration, a publication-commit write and a verifier step to that window raises its risk without closing any gap that is reachable before ED-02.

The gap is real: a principal who can write to the DB can forge an artifact plus every recomputed hash. It is bounded by the V15 immutability triggers and by the fact that nothing is released yet. It must be closed before the first deployed replay, and the gate below enforces that.

followUpStoryGate.placement: @po places a follow-up story ('artifact HMAC, Vault Transit'; the ID is @po's choice, not invented here) in the STUDIO-OBSERVED wave.
followUpStoryGate.entryGate: Do not start until E1-E4 below are CONFIRMED by Platform/SRE with ticket references.
followUpStoryGate.exitGate: The story lands before any deployed profile (dev cluster, UAT or prod) replays an observed revision for a pilot. Otherwise the external OBS-010 security review must accept its absence as a named residual, with the owner recorded. It may not be dropped by omission.

designForFollowUp_bindingNow.seam: One narrow interface, ArtifactIntegrityKeys { String sign(byte[] input); boolean verify(byte[] input, String tag); }, with exactly two production-reachable implementations: VaultTransitArtifactIntegrityKeys and NoArtifactIntegrityKeys. The test profile adds a third, an in-memory test fake, selectable only there, in the same way as the existing fake Vault provider. No generic 'crypto provider' abstraction.
designForFollowUp_bindingNow.config: A separate prefix studio.artifact-integrity.* with keys provider (none | vault-transit), transit-mount, key-name and min-key-version. Address, namespace, token-file and timeouts are inherited from studio.secrets.vault.hashicorp.* unless they are overridden. A separate token-file property is allowed, so Platform can issue a least-privilege token. All values are environment-driven. Nothing is hardcoded.
designForFollowUp_bindingNow.calls: Sign: POST /v1/{transit-mount}/hmac/{key-name}/sha2-256 with input = base64("studio-artifact-hmac-v1" || 0x00 || canonical-v1(binding)). Verify: POST /v1/{transit-mount}/verify/{key-name}/sha2-256 with the same input and the stored tag, so the comparison happens inside Vault. Store the tag string verbatim ('vault:vN:...'). artifact_hmac_key_version is N, parsed from the tag and checked against it on read.
designForFollowUp_bindingNow.failClosed: If Transit is unreachable or times out at replay, refuse with the existing transient 503 VAULT_UNAVAILABLE path that the guided code already uses (not a new code). A verify=false, a missing tag, or a key version below min-key-version refuses with the existing 409 EVIDENCE_MISMATCH. The check is never skipped. The note's 'VAULT_UNAVAILABLE-style' wording must name VAULT_UNAVAILABLE exactly.

localDevTestBehaviour.test: The in-memory fake generates a random key per Spring context, and the key is never persisted or logged. ITs prove real sign/verify semantics: a tampered artifact with recomputed hashes is refused, a missing tag is refused, an outage simulated by the fake throwing is refused and not skipped, and a re-sign verifies before it overwrites. Test names and Javadoc must say 'fake key service'. No test or document may claim Transit was exercised.
localDevTestBehaviour.local: provider=none is allowed. Publication writes a NULL tag, and verify refuses a NULL tag unless studio.artifact-integrity.allow-unsigned-replay=true. That flag is honoured only when the active profile is local or test, and start-up refuses it anywhere else. Every unsigned replay logs WARN {revisionId, reason=UNSIGNED}, and ExecutionReadinessService reports artifactIntegrity=NOT_CONFIGURED. A developer may point at a local `vault server -dev` with Transit enabled; this is optional and not mandatory tooling.
localDevTestBehaviour.devClusterUatProd: A deployed profile treats provider=none as 'no observed replay': revisions publish without a tag and every replay refuses with EVIDENCE_MISMATCH. Start-up does NOT fail, so non-Studio Checks features keep running. This matches the existing convention that the Vault adapter is off until connected. No deployed profile may set allow-unsigned-replay.
localDevTestBehaviour.noFakeProdClaims: Until E1-E4 are CONFIRMED, no story, runbook, helm comment or QA gate may describe artifact integrity as 'enabled', 'enforced' or 'signed' for any deployed environment.

rotation.routine: Platform/SRE runs `transit/keys/{key}/rotate`, and new publications sign with the latest version. The backend's re-sign job does verify(old tag) → sign(latest) → compare-and-set on (revision_id, old tag). It never re-signs a tag that does not verify, so it cannot launder a forgery. When every row carries version ≥ v, Platform/SRE raises studio.artifact-integrity.min-key-version to v through deployment configuration.
rotation.retireAuthority: The backend-side min-key-version floor is the authoritative retirement control, because it is under this repository's control and testable with the fake. Transit's min_decryption_version may also be raised, but its effect on HMAC verify is UNCONFIRMED (E8) and the design must not depend on it.
rotation.emergency: On suspected key compromise, raise min-key-version above the compromised version (a config change plus a rolling restart, with no Vault call needed) and rotate in Transit. Revisions on the old version refuse EVIDENCE_MISMATCH, are reported by id, and must be re-verified out of band and re-published (design note §5).

externalDependencies_UNCONFIRMED.item: The Transit secrets engine is enabled on the platform Vault namespace that serves this service, and its mount path is known.
A dedicated key exists for this purpose, created non-exportable with deletion_allowed=false (a key type that supports HMAC).
A Vault policy for the backend identity grants only 'update' on {mount}/hmac/{key}/* and {mount}/verify/{key}/*. It grants no keys/*, rotate, export or config capability.
The backend's Vault auth method and token delivery, whether the same mounted-token pattern as KV or another method. This is the same open question as ED-02.
A Vault audit device is enabled and covers Transit calls.
Transit latency/availability SLO, set against the replay latency budget for one verify call per replay.
Ownership and cadence of the rotation runbook (the rotate step and the min-key-version raise).
Semantics of min_decryption_version for HMAC verify on the platform's Vault version (informational; the design does not rely on it).

ruling2_admissionRefusalCodes.verdict: RATIFIED, all five items. None of them changes what the runner or an operator sees for real traffic. The oracles changed because the tests moved off the deleted legacy route onto the observed route, whose codes are unchanged since HEAD. That is exactly what AR-3 meant by 'the observed path's codes are unchanged'. One documentation fix is REQUIRED (2.R1). One contract residual is recorded (2.N1).
verifiedFacts: The runner never called the legacy route. studio-runner/src/reporting/admissionClient.ts:66 posts only to /observed-admission.

The runner collapses every non-200 admission answer into ObservedRefusal('AUTHORIZATION_EXPIRED') (admissionClient.ts:67-68), so it never reads the refusal code. ATTEMPT_SUPERSEDED, EXECUTION_SETTLED, FORBIDDEN_SCOPE and CANCELLED all produce identical runner behaviour.

The observed-path codes predate B14. At HEAD, ObservedReplayAuthorization.prepareAdmission already returned 403 FORBIDDEN_SCOPE on any binding/attemptId mismatch, and check() already returned 409 CANCELLED when 'cancel_requested_at IS NOT NULL OR state='DONE'' (HEAD lines 313-316). The working tree adds 'OR revoked_at IS NOT NULL' from earlier wave work, which is outside B14's P1 scope. ObservedAdmissionSecurityIT.expiredGrantAndCancelledExecutionStopBeforeAccountOrCas pins CANCELLED on the observed route.

AdmissionCasService.claimObserved takes 'FOR UPDATE OF l,e' on the ledger and execution rows before it calls observed.check(binding) and then claimAt. Because cancel and DONE are refused by check() under that lock, claimAt.refusal()'s cancel-close branch (closeWithError CANCELLED + EXECUTION_SETTLED) and its DONE → EXECUTION_SETTLED branch cannot be reached through the only remaining caller.

AR-3 b itself ruled these oracles (ar-2-3-obs014.json): aSupersededAttemptIsRefused → '403 FORBIDDEN_SCOPE … ledger unchanged' (line 216); aSettledExecutionIsRefused → '409 EXECUTION_SETTLED, or the observed path's earlier refusal; record the actual' (line 218); CancelIT → 'may change from EXECUTION_SETTLED to the observed path's CANCELLED … Record the actual. The execution MUST still end ERROR/CANCELLED' (line 238). S-7 also allows it: a refusal with zero writes → update the oracle by name and record it.

B14's run, as recorded in the ledger: AdmissionCasIT 14/0, CancelIT 16/0, StudioAuthorizationIT 28/0, ObservedAdmissionSecurityIT 100/0 (parameterised invocations), and RecoveryIT 25/0 after the fix. These are ledger statements; @architect did not re-run them.

items.change: Stale attempt: ATTEMPT_SUPERSEDED (legacy CAS) → 403 FORBIDDEN_SCOPE (observed prepareAdmission)
items.ruling: RATIFIED. This is the oracle AR-3 itself ruled, not a deviation. The refusal happens before any lock or write, and the ledger is unchanged (asserted).
items.runnerOperatorImpact: None. The runner maps both to AUTHORIZATION_EXPIRED. The operator sees no admission code, and the execution row is untouched.

items.ruling: RATIFIED under AR-3's 'record the actual'. Refusing a DONE row as CANCELLED is imprecise wording on an internal callback, but it is the observed path's pre-existing answer and nobody consumes it. Zero writes, and the execution's settled status is unchanged.
items.runnerOperatorImpact: None. The runner collapses the code, and the operator-visible execution status stays whatever settled it.
items.notRequired: Splitting check() into CANCELLED vs EXECUTION_SETTLED is NOT required and is not to be done in 014. It would change the observed path, which AR-3 said stays unchanged.

items.change: Cancel before admission: EXECUTION_SETTLED with an immediate ERROR/CANCELLED close (legacy) → 409 CANCELLED with zero writes, then RunningReaper.findUnfinishedCancels ends the execution ERROR/CANCELLED after the cancel margin
items.ruling: RATIFIED. AR-3's mandatory property, 'execution MUST still end ERROR/CANCELLED', holds and CancelIT asserts it.
items.runnerOperatorImpact: Not a regression. Real runs only ever used /observed-admission, so in practice they already settled through the reaper: time-to-terminal = the effective cancel margin (≈92 s with shipped defaults per application.yml:328, inferred from the comment and not measured). Only the deleted legacy route closed immediately, and it had no runner caller. The cancel is honoured: no browser authority is granted (no receipt, no admission_id).
items.observationNotRequirement: Settling a refused-cancelled admission immediately on the observed path would improve operator latency. It would be an observed-path behaviour change (prepareAdmission runs outside a transaction by design), so it is out of 014. @po may place it with OBS-009 runtime hardening if wanted. It is not owed.

items.ruling: RATIFIED (re-point over drop was the correct auto-decision). These cases test properties of StrictInternalBodyReader (real token required, no quoting of private malformed values), and /progress is that reader's only surviving consumer (StudioInternalController.bodyReader). The observed-admission route uses a different parser (observedContracts.parseWire, StudioInternalController:76), and the same class already covers it (rawMalformedAndDuplicateJsonRefuseBeforeStoredAuthority, malformedUtf8CannotTurnIntoReplacementCharacterAuthority, extraIdentityOrPrivateMetadataCannotBeSmuggledIntoObservedBody, observedByteBoundDoesNotExposeTheBody…), so no coverage is lost.
items.condition: Record the old → new names in the story's P1 entry. This is already done in story Change Log 0.1.6 / Dev Agent Record P1 and in ledger t1a.testsChanged; @qa confirms it at the gate.

items.change: RecoveryIT.theDispatchCounterCanReachTwoAndTheReconciledLedgerStateIsWhatStopsIt: admission at statement level (StudioDispatchLedgerStatements.admit in a TransactionTemplate) instead of admitObserved
items.ruling: RATIFIED under the AR-3 b precedent (AdmissionCasIT.observedSqlCannotBorrow…). The property under test is reconciliation of the dispatch counter and ledger state, not admission. Observed admission writes the V15-immutable observed_admission_receipt, which the test's 'neutralise one term' control cannot clear, so the control would no longer isolate the property. The assertions are unchanged. A comment at RecoveryIT:330-334 states why. AdmissionCasService exposes no public claim() (verified), so no legacy entry was reintroduced for tests.
items.condition: None beyond @qa recording it as an S-7-class re-point.

requiredFix.what: Correct the Javadoc of AdmissionCasService.claimAt (and, if it repeats the claim, the @Transactional(noRollbackFor) note on claimObserved). It still says 'The one refusal that writes: a cancel recorded before the admission arrived … closes the execution ERROR / CANCELLED and answers EXECUTION_SETTLED'. Through claimObserved, that branch is unreachable: check() refuses cancel/DONE first, under the same row lock. The Javadoc must say that the cancel-close and DONE branches of refusal() are defence-in-depth, not reached through claimObserved because check() refuses those rows CANCELLED under the same lock, and that a cancelled admission is settled by RunningReaper.
requiredFix.behaviourChange: None. Comment only. Do not delete the branches in 014. They are cheap defence and AR-3 kept refusal() intact.
requiredFix.why: Without the fix, a future reader will believe the observed path closes cancelled admissions immediately, which is the exact misreading this ratification resolves.

residualRecorded.owner: C lane (contract owner), next contract-touching unit; not owed by 014
residualRecorded.what: openapi.yaml:260 x-conflict-codes for the observed-admission 409 still lists ATTEMPT_SUPERSEDED and EXECUTION_SETTLED. After P1 the observed route is inferred never to emit them. Inferred, not proven: ATTEMPT_SUPERSEDED would need the ledger attempt to diverge from the stored binding inside the lock. The list is a descriptive superset and the runner ignores the codes, so it is harmless. Trim it only when the C lane next re-anchors the digest anyway, so the re-anchor cost is not paid for this alone.

tradeOffs: Transit vs KMS: Transit wins on no new SDK, a single outage domain and a single audit trail. It loses by inheriting ED-02's open status. KMS would add a dependency and a second coupling, and its availability is equally unverified.

Defer vs promote now: deferring leaves the DB-writer forgery gap open in pre-release builds, bounded by V15 triggers and by the fact that no deployed replay is allowed. Promoting now would ship a control proven only against a fake and widen the riskiest S3 window.

Ratify vs restore legacy codes: restoring the legacy codes would need either the deleted route (rejected by the 012A gate, because it admitted without observed authorization) or changes to the observed path's refusals (which AR-3 said stay unchanged). Neither code is consumed by the runner.
autoDecisions: [AUTO-DECISION] Promote AC-11 into 014? → No (reason: the real provider is not connected or confirmed in any environment, a fake-only fail-closed control would be a false production claim, and 014's S3 window is already the riskiest step).

[AUTO-DECISION] Deployed profile with provider=none: fail start-up or refuse replay? → Refuse replay and keep start-up (reason: non-Studio Checks features must not go down for a Studio-only control; this matches the existing Vault-off convention).
[AUTO-DECISION] Delete the now-unreachable cancel/DONE branches in claimAt.refusal()? → No, fix the Javadoc only (reason: defence-in-depth at zero cost; AR-3 kept refusal() intact).
